Description: Third-party webhooks are accepted, logged durably and buffered at peak load (FR-002, NFR-001)
Only correctly signed, non-duplicate events enter the system (FR-005)
Events reach internal services, failures are retried with exponential backoff and dead-lettered when retries run out (FR-001, FR-003)
Developers register sources and routes; operators watch delivery health (FR-004, NFR-002)
As an integration developer, I want the gateway to accept a third-party webhook over HTTPS and reply 202 Accepted immediately, so that the sender does not time out or resend the event.

As an integration developer, I want every inbound event (source, headers, payload, timestamp, event ID) written to a durable log before it is acknowledged, so that no accepted event is ever lost and I can audit what arrived.
As a system operator, I want the ingestion endpoint to buffer bursts of up to 2,500 requests per second with 99.999% reliability, so that peak traffic from providers is never dropped.
As an integration developer, I want each webhook's HMAC-SHA256 signature checked against the source's secret and invalid ones rejected with 401, so that spoofed events never reach internal services.
As an integration developer, I want an event resent with the same event ID to be delivered only once, so that internal services do not process the same event twice.

Summary: Route and deliver event to target
Description: As an integration developer, I want each accepted event forwarded to the internal endpoint registered for its event type, so that my service receives the events it subscribed to.

Summary: Retry failed deliveries with exponential backoff
Description: As an integration developer, I want failed deliveries retried after 1 s, 2 s, 4 s and 8 s with each attempt logged, so that short outages of my service do not lose events.

Summary: Dead-letter queue with replay and discard
Description: As a system operator, I want events that fail 5 times moved to a dead-letter queue where I can inspect, replay or discard them, so that failed events are recoverable instead of retried forever.

As an integration developer, I want to register a webhook source with its signing secret and map event types to target URLs and retry policies, so that I can connect new providers without code changes.
As a system operator, I want a dashboard showing delivery success rate, retry count, dead-letter queue size and p95 latency, refreshed every 10 seconds, so that I can spot failing targets quickly.
